SAME FOOTPRINT / TWO ROOT SOCKETS

A precise place to rest.

The lower frame keeps its dimensions. The 5 cm tooth receives its own smaller split socket, beneath repeated equilateral bevels and spherical junctions.

Tooth: 1 MPa crown pressure, rigid root constraints. Support: CAD self-weight plus 3 × g tooth gravity. Simultaneous visibility does not imply a coupled tooth–support solution.

Choosing a file format

3MFMillimetres, full indexed geometry, shared stress palette, per-size physical metadata and source record. Keep native colour support enabled when importing.

STLComplete surface in binary STL. Select millimetres on import. STL carries geometry only; its numerical field and material properties are in the accompanying JSON/NPZ.

OBJComplete indexed surface with its matching MTL palette. Extract the ZIP, keep OBJ and MTL together, and set the scene unit to millimetres.

A visible field. A traceable method.

Root retention

The R2.1 negative seat wraps the root shoulders. A fixed rear seat joins the frame; locating pins and two M2.5 screws close the front cap to hard stops. Clear soft pads take up play.

Shear & bending method

G = E / [2(1 + ν)]
δb = FL³ / (3EI)
δs = FL / (κGA)

The frame uses spatial Timoshenko beams. Foot translations are constrained, rotations free; no sliding is assumed. Force and moment act at P. Assumed resin density: 1.18 g/cm³; fasteners: 2 g.

ν=0.38, reduction 0.5 and Kt=2 are design assumptions. G describes stiffness. Fracture, pull-out, creep and impact require independent checks.

From coupons to full assembly

  1. Test clearance. Clean and fully cure all six coupons, then fit them to the finished tooth.
  2. Print separately. Slice frame and cap individually; protect negative surfaces, pins and holes.
  3. Insert from the front. Place the root in the rear seat, add clear soft pads and close to the hard stops.
  4. Inspect the print. Check foot coplanarity, paint clearance and retention under a gentle touch before progressive testing.
